label: Fires at D1 late in episode when S1 believed good and last reached S1, esp. after rewarded a1.
short_terms: (phase == D1) * (belief_lo > 0) * np.square(ep_trial) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * np.square(ep_trial) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S1 r") * np.square(ep_trial)
terms: (phase == D1) * (belief > 0.5) * ep_trial ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * ep_trial ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 1) * (prev_action == 1) * ep_trial ;; (phase == D1) * (belief > 0.5) * ep_trial**2 ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * ep_trial**2 ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 1) * (prev_action == 1) * ep_trial**2 ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 1) * (prev_reward == 1) * ep_trial ;; (phase == D1) * (tv("state", -2) == 1) * ep_trial
explanation: Silent at GO and D2. At D1 it is near-binary (about 1.2-1.5 when it fires, else 0) and fires only late in the episode (timing baseline rises from trial ~40 to ~90). Beyond timing, it fires when the previous trial reached S1 (S2 suppresses it) and the observer believes S1 is good, most strongly after a1 -> S1 (common), and more after a run of S1 trials; previous reward matters little once state is accounted for. The effect grows with episode trial (multiplicative with timing, fit best with ep_trial squared). The free fit adds linear+quadratic time and the trial-before state, a small gain (dev 0.315 vs 0.288). Much variance remains: firing vs not firing within otherwise similar late D1 S1 steps is not fully predicted, and the first window trial lacks a previous-trial pattern.
